From 6cbba46934aefdfb5d171e0a95aec06c24f7ca30 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 15:44:40 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net: liquidio: Fix off-by-one error in VF setup_nic_devices()
 cleanup

In setup_nic_devices(), the initialization loop jumps to the label
setup_nic_dev_free on failure. The current cleanup loop while(i--)
skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak.

Fix this by changing the loop to iterate from the current index i
down to 0.

Compile tested only. Issue found using code review.

Fixes: 846b46873eeb ("liquidio CN23XX: VF offload features")
Suggested-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Kory Maincent <kory.maincent@bootlin.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260128154440.278369-4-zilin@seu.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c
index e02942dbbcce..43c595f3b84e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c
@@ -2212,11 +2212,11 @@ static int setup_nic_devices(struct octeon_device *octeon_dev)
 
 setup_nic_dev_free:
 
-	while (i--) {
+	do {
 		dev_err(&octeon_dev->pci_dev->dev,
 			"NIC ifidx:%d Setup failed\n", i);
 		liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i);
-	}
+	} while (i--);
 
 setup_nic_dev_done:
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an off-by-one error in the cleanup path of `setup_nic_devices()` in `drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c`.

**Modification per file:**
- `drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_vf_main.c`: Changed the cleanup loop from `while (i--)` to `do { ... } while (i--)`. This ensures that the loop body executes for the failing index `i` before decrementing, instead of skipping that index and causing a memory leak.

**Relationship:**
The single-file change corrects the loop logic: the original `while (i--)` would decrement `i` before running the body for the current index, meaning if the failure occurred at index `i`, that index was never cleaned up. The new `do-while` runs the body first for the current `i`, then decrements, so the failed index is properly cleaned up. This directly fixes the off-by-one memory leak described in the commit message.
